newsitem.title: POLAND: TENNIS-AUSTRIA'S PAULUS WINS WARSAW CUP.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-AUSTRIA'S PAULUS WINS WARSAW CUP.

text.p: Austrian Barbara Paulus won her second Warsaw Cup in three years on Sunday, beating last year's winner Henrieta Nagoyova of Slovakia 6-4 6-4 in the final.
Paulus, the top seed and ranked 16 in the world, came back from 4-0 down in the second set to win the $165,000 clay-court tournament.
"Maybe I was a bit lucky to win after being down 4-0, 40-15 in the second set but I am very happy," Paulus, 26, told the 2,500-strong crowd.
"I tried to run her from corner to corner to tire her out for a possible third set but it worked so well that I won," she said.
The 18-year-old Slovak said Paulus had hit effectively from the baseline but said that fatigue also had a role as both women had played their semifinals earlier on Sunday, following rain on Saturday.
"Paulus had stronger legs, she is very fit physically but I think that my reaching the final was a success," said Nagoyova, ranked 39th in the world before the tournament.
Earlier on Sunday, Paulus had beaten Spaniard Virginia Ruano Pascual 6-2 6-1 in her semifinal and sixth seed Nagoyova had defeated second seed Ruxandra Dragomir of Romania 6-4 7-5.
